eyebrow: The memory math, for a 7B model in FP16
code:
weights          = 7B params x 2 bytes  ~= 14 GB
gradients        = 7B params x 2 bytes  ~= 14 GB
adam optimizer   = 7B params x 8 bytes  ~= 56 GB   (FP32 momentum + variance)
activations      = varies with batch size / seq length
                                          ------------
                 total (full fine-tune) ~= 80-100+ GB
caption: More than a single 80 GB A100 or H100 — before you've even raised batch size.

eyebrow: Why LoRA, quantization, and ZeRO exist
code:
# Direct responses to the memory wall, not a compute shortage:
#  - LoRA:            train small adapter weights, not the full model
#  - 8-bit/4-bit quantization: shrink weight footprint
#  - Gradient checkpointing:   recompute activations instead of storing them
#  - DeepSpeed ZeRO / FSDP:    shard state across multiple GPUs
caption: "CUDA out of memory" is the most common training failure in practice.

code:
# Capacity:  total VRAM on the card (e.g. 80 GB on an A100-80GB)
#            -> decides whether the working set fits AT ALL
#
# Bandwidth: HBM2e on A100 ~2 TB/s, HBM3 on H100 higher
#            -> decides how fast cores get fed, not whether it fits
caption: Capacity-bound and bandwidth-bound jobs both look like 'the GPU is the bottleneck' — the fixes differ.
